lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Piano for Empty Rooms. Ninety three point oh five. Please. Don't get up.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This is Piano for Empty Rooms. Music, for rooms nobody has entered yet.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Piano for Empty Rooms. The door is open slightly. It always has been.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: You're listening to Piano for Empty Rooms, from the unvisited wing. Quietly, please.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Piano for Empty Rooms. It's late. The rooms don't mind. They have nowhere to be.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Piano for Empty Rooms. Nobody is here.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: That's the idea.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This next piece is for the linen room on the third floor. It was finished in the spring. Nobody has been in since.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It has shelves, and a window, and it has never been told what it's for.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This one is for the guest room. It's been made up for a guest for a very long time. Fresh sheets every Sunday. A glass of water on the nightstand.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The guest hasn't come. The room isn't upset. It's ready. That's all.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I don't go into the rooms. I'm not supposed to. I sit outside, in the corridor, and the piano plays, and I listen at the doors.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It's a good arrangement. Nobody disturbs anybody.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The piano is playing itself again tonight. It doesn't need me. I've been told I'm not needed, by several people, quite kindly.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I come anyway. Someone should hear it.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: There's a ballroom on the fourth floor. Sprung floor. Chandeliers. A little balcony for the band. Nobody has ever danced there. Not once.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The floor is perfect. Not a single scuff. This is a waltz for it. You don't have to dance. Neither does the floor.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Something happened in the east wing this week. Footprints, in the dust. One person. To the window, and back. They stood at the window for a while, I think. Long enough to see the garden.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: We've taken the east room off the schedule. It's a visited room now. It'll be all right. It looked out of the window too.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: People ask what a caretaker does, in rooms nobody uses. Mostly, I dust the light.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It comes in through the tall windows and lies on the floorboards, and the dust settles in it. I don't move the dust. I just make sure the light is still there in the morning.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This piece is for the room behind the bookcase. Nobody has found it. I know it's there, because the corridor is three feet longer than the rooms add up to.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I haven't looked. It's not my place. But it deserves music, the same as the others.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The door at the back of the music room is open about an inch. It has been since I came here. I've never closed it.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I don't know if it's an invitation or a draught. I've decided it's both. That seems kindest.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Morning, now. The light is coming round the east side. In a minute it will reach the piano, and the piano will play a little brighter.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It always does. It doesn't know it does. Don't tell it.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: If you're the one on the ship, on the night watch. I expect there's a room aboard that nobody uses. A storeroom. A spare cabin. A cupboard with one chair in it.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This one is for it. Leave the door the way you found it.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This is for a waiting room, in a station that was built, and finished, and never opened. Rows of benches. A clock that somebody winds.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Nobody is waiting there. Which, if you think about it, is the best kind of waiting room.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This one is for the attic of a house on a road that was only finished last week. Nobody has been up the ladder yet. It's warm up there, and quiet, and it smells of new wood.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: One day there'll be boxes. Not yet.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: This is Dust Sheets, on Piano for Empty Rooms. The chairs are covered. The lamps are off. Mind the rug.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I've been round with the dust sheets. The chairs in the drawing room are covered now, and they look like small ghosts having a meeting.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I don't mind. They're only furniture, being shy.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The grandfather clock in the hall has been stopped since before I came. I don't wind it. I think it's resting.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I just like to stand near it, at about this time, and agree with it.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It's the middle of the night. This is the Unvisited Hours. Nobody will come now. We can all relax.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: At this hour the house makes small sounds. The pipes. The stairs settling. A window easing in its frame.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: People think a house is quiet when it's empty. It isn't. It's just talking to itself, now that it can.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Three in the morning. Every room in the wing is empty, every door closed, except the one. The piano is playing for all of them at once.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: That takes some doing. It manages.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Good morning. This is First Light in the East Wing. The sun is in the windows. The piano knows.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The sun has reached the ballroom. Long gold stripes from the windows, right across the floor, and the chandelier throwing little lights on the ceiling.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: If anyone saw it, they'd gasp. Nobody will. It does it anyway. That's the whole idea, really.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Morning on the east side. The footprints are still there in the dust, from the other week. I haven't swept them.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The room seems to like them.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It's the time of year when people ask me if the empty rooms are haunted. No. A haunted room has somebody in it.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: These rooms are waiting for somebody. That's a different thing entirely. It's much less noise.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Someone has left a carved pumpkin at the end of the west corridor. A candle in it. Lit. I didn't light it. Nobody has been in.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It's been glowing all week. I've decided not to look into it. It's company.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: They say a moon has gone. Nobody knows which.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: There's a space in the sky now. Nobody has been in it. I'll add it to the schedule.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The corridor smells of toast. There's no kitchen in this wing.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: I've left the doors open a little. So the rooms can have some.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The piano is playing a tune that everyone seems to know.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It stops at the same place each time. Then it waits. I think it's waiting for a room to hum the rest.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Three knocks. On the door at the back of the music room. The one that's open about an inch.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: Nobody there. I said, come in. It's open. It has always been open.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The light came through the window a colour I've never seen. It lay on the floor of the music room for a moment.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: The first thing ever to visit that room. I've taken it off the schedule.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: A pigeon walked down the west corridor. It stopped at every door, as if it knew which ones were empty.

lines.speaker: The Caretaker
lines.text: It listened at the music room for a while. Then it left. It didn't disturb the dust.
